items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I contributed another arrangement that I did for them... It was Doc Reiker, who used to take the band is conduct... He had been in it since its beginning

ctx.x: be an advancement for me to go with the Whiteman band. There were more instruments, arrangements, a lot more possibilities in the band and as far as Trumbauer and Bix were concerned, it would be logical for them to go with Rollini, but I tried to get them to go with Paul, and no, they didn't want to go there.

So that was my next move, anyway. But the band, in the meantime, as I understand it, they left here and went to Roseland and that's where they made "Clementine," at that particular time. I contributed another arrangement that I did for them. That was strictly a head arrangement. If anybody should have should be Doc Ryker, credit for it, it was Doc Reiker, who used to take the band is conduct and where they were going and what they were going to do very seriously. He was afraid it would break up. He was afraid the…

So he would be around and he would, I guess he took the orchestration and told Trumbauer to get his saxophone thing, work out a saxophone chorus and then it would give -- well, Bix didn't have -- tell them to woodshed, we had a term then go over in your corner and woodshed these parts and then we'd come back and put the whole thing together.

items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I just got a letter not long ago from Doc Reiker Ryker who has been bugged by some writer and he said, 'You were there on the date...'

ctx.x: No, sir. That doesn't make sense anyway. Well, anyway, but Ludwig he really knew the tempo, he had been playing it for a long time. He had a lot to do with the band, and I'm just wondering what happened between him and Fletcher. They traded off a few new arrangements, so the first thing I know my Blue Room and a couple other things are being played by Fletcher, later, and we had a "Stampede," and

a couple of other things." Stampede" was supposed to have been recorded -- I just got a letter not long ago from Doc Reiker Ryker who has been bugged by some writer and he said, "You were there on the date, but ~~ and he said that you made Stampede, and I get credit for the arrangement. ^ Which You know, I didn't do ^ an's of course -- I am pretty sure I think it's Redmond's composition.

So I wrote back and told him, "Forget about things like that." The guy told him they had made it and I wasn't there at the recording so maybe they did n't make it; but some young kid tells me now that they made it but and it was rejected, so I don't know anything about it. But I think we had a couple other things too that were switched around between the bands.
